data.gender_notes: Riyansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Lord Rama, a divine name which was born to King Dasharatha and Queen Kausalya. He is considered as the seventh avatar of Lord Vishnu. He is an embodiment of truth, morality, and courage. The name Riyansh carries the meaning “Lord Rama” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Riyansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord rama and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Riyansh belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Rama.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Riyansh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Riyansh" is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Ram' which is synonymous with Lord Rama. Rama is an inspiring figure from Hindu mythology and is known for his unwavering commitment to duty, truth, and morality. He is also depicted as a righteous and courageous king. The name "Riyansh" thus, evokes images of strength, honor, and loyalty.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Rama is believed to be a symbol of the supreme divine being. The name "Riyansh," which means "Lord Rama," thus holds deep spiritual significance. It symbolizes the divine presence of Lord Rama in one's life, and instills a sense of faith, devotion, and spiritual growth. The name is a constant reminder of Lord Rama's teachings of duty, truth, and morality.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Riyansh: Radiant and Victorious. A name embodying the spirit of triumph and brilliance, symbolizing one's inner light shining through victories in life.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Riyansh remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
